answer.question: Are we on pace to hit goal, and where do we land by election day if nothing changes?
answer.answer:
We are ahead of pace to date, but if nothing changes the program lands at 57329 doors on Election Day, 3303 short of the 60632 goal.
- Pace to date: 33503 doors against a goal to date of 32431, 103.3% of goal to date (Sep 21 to Oct 18) [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Last 7 days (Oct 12 to 18): 1489.1 doors a day on average, with 16 knocking days left [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Projection: 57329 doors, 94.6% of the 60632 goal, a shortfall of 3303 doors (projected_vs_goal -3303) [table:v_office_pace_total]
- How it's worked out: doors to date plus the last 7 days' average daily doors times the knocking days left; we miss goal when the projection is below the total goal [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]

cases.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?

facts.name: doors we can knock in the days left

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
Ask the client for more doors: at our current pace we will knock more doors than the untouched doors left in our turf, so we run out of first-pass turf; a second pass is the fallback.
- Capacity for the rest of the program: 1489.1 doors a day over the last 7 days x 16 knocking days left, the 23826 doors between the 33503 to date and the 57329 projected [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10393 of 41853 turf doors [table:v_office_pace_total]
- By office, untouched doors: Eastgate 1183, Northside 1114, Harbor 8096; Eastgate (380.7 a day) and Northside (621 a day) will run out of turf, while Harbor (487.4 a day, 7799 doors projected from here) still has more untouched doors than capacity and should keep working its turf [table:v_office_pace]
- Rule: when capacity is larger than the untouched doors, ask for more doors first, since new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate; second passes on not-home doors contact at roughly half that rate, so they are the fallback [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]

cases.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's sheet counts attempts before QC rollbacks, while our dashboard counts doors once per day with rollbacks removed; on Oct 12 most of the gap is Eastgate's rolled-back flash knocking shift.
- Program, Oct 12: the client sheet shows 1484 "doors" (attempts) vs our 1281 doors [table:v_daily_doors_total]
- Eastgate: 498 reported vs 342 doors; 142 of the 498 attempts were rolled back, the rest of the gap is repeat attempts; contacts 110 reported vs 77 [table:v_daily_doors]
- Harbor: 428 reported vs 406 doors, 0 rolled back, so the gap is repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- Northside: 558 reported vs 533 doors, 0 rolled back, so the gap is repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- Why: the daily report is pulled at the end of the day before any rollback; the gap is repeat attempts at the same door plus attempts later rolled back, and a large gap almost always means a rollback [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

Householding is recording results for several units or voters at one address from a single conversation, instead of knocking each unit. A shift is flagged when 4 or more units at the same address are marked canvassed within 5 minutes with identical survey answers. Householded results are not rolled back automatically; the field lead reviews them with the canvasser.

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock; a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart.
- Threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks under 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back, so those knocks no longer count as doors or contacts; a whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data marked rolled back, and rollbacks never change a client report already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- Every open flag needs a field lead conversation before the canvasser's next shift; two or more flash knocking or householding flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift, using the timestamped evidence on the flag. After the conversation the flag is marked reviewed. Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director.

The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.
